what_matters.head: SK Hynix fell about 9% and Samsung about 8% by 13:05 Seoul time, after China's CXMT said it plans to launch a denser kind of server memory by the end of 2026. The Kospi was down 7.2% around midday, its lowest level since July.
what_matters.detail: CXMT's president, Cao Kanyu, made the announcement at an industry event in Shanghai over the weekend: new DDR5 server memory modules built on a denser '4F²' memory-cell design. The news first hit on Monday, when both stocks fell about 4% in Seoul and Micron fell 3.9% in New York; Monday's Korean fall, which yesterday's briefing could not explain, came after it.

what_matters.head: The day moves shown below for SK Hynix, Samsung, UOB and DBS are measured from the wrong close. Yahoo's price history skips Monday for every Seoul and Singapore name, and the data run took Monday for a market holiday.
what_matters.detail: Both markets traded on Monday. Measured from Monday's close, UOB is up about 1.3%, not 2.9%, and DBS about 0.9%, not 1.7%; SK Hynix's and Samsung's true falls are above. OCBC's figure is close. Their five-day moves and × usual sizes also span one session too many, so UOB's 2.4 × usual is not real.

what_matters.head: Wednesday brings the MAS policy statement in the morning, ASML's results at 13:00 SGT and US consumer prices for September at 20:30. TSMC reports on Thursday at 14:00.
what_matters.detail: MAS has not announced a time; 08:00 SGT is the calendar's. The companies' forecasts and the options-implied moves are under Earnings.

after_data.text: Elon Musk wrote on X on Monday that once China learns to make a product, its ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined, but that advanced memory 'will be harder to solve'. Micron, SK Hynix's US shares and SanDisk fell a further 1–2% after the close, Benzinga reported. Those after-hours falls are not in Monday's US prices.

Navitas said after Monday's close (16:15 New York time) that it has built a 24-kilowatt power board for AI data centres with Nvidia, on show at the OCP summit this week. Its shares rose 3.0% after hours. Not in Monday's US prices.

latest.tape_note: US stocks were mixed on Monday: the S&P 500 slipped 0.1% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.7%, while the Dow rose 0.4%. Chip stocks fell again: SOXX, the chip-stock fund, lost 2.6% on the day, about its usual swing, and 7.6% over five days. The US dollar index rose 0.4%, a little more than its usual day, and oil rose 2.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield held at 5.24%, with the bond market shut for Columbus Day. The US dollar was flat against the Singapore dollar.
latest.tonight: No high-impact US release is scheduled tonight. The OCP Global Summit, where the big cloud companies and chip makers discuss data-centre hardware, runs in San Jose until Thursday. The MAS policy statement is due early on Wednesday, Singapore time.
